items.status: OPEN — filed 2026-10-05 (the owner's item; added to editor-47 with E267, Order 47)
items.title: the "import it first" steer spells a NESTED module by its leaf name — `unknown struct: ProxySignal; import it first (`import pkg::proxy_signal::ProxySignal;`)` where the type lives at `pkg::lib::proxy_signal::ProxySignal`, so the suggested import does not resolve
items.body:
The owner's report, from kolt (`src/lib/proxy_signal.vl`): the steer on an unknown name prints `import pkg::proxy_signal::ProxySignal;`; the real path is `pkg::lib::proxy_signal::ProxySignal`.

Cause (read in the source at next @99285bc4, `crates/vilan-core/src/analyzer.rs` near the `"; import it first (`import {root}::{module}::{name};`)"` format): the steer walks the modules for a definition of the name and formats `{root}::{module.name}::{name}`, where `module.name` is the module's own LEAF name, not its path from the package root. Two consequences: (1) any module below the top level gets an import that cannot be written; (2) the ambiguity check compares leaf names (`*existing == module.name`), so two different modules with the same leaf name in different directories count as ONE hit and the steer names neither correctly.

Fix: spell the module's full path from its root (the same spelling the loader accepts; solver-47 fixed the B515 warning's import the same way for nested std modules, from std's export index), compare hits by module identity, and check the std branch for nested std modules (`std::reactive::…`, `std::web::…`). Same root as E267 (auto-import and the add-import fix read only a package's top level); the doc comment above the function says completion and the add-import quick fix read the same data, so one fix should serve all three. Pin: a package with `src/lib/thing.vl` exporting a struct, an unknown use elsewhere, the steer's import compiles when pasted.
